content: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the likelihood of severe side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your healthcare provider and pharmacist. Certain medications may influence the elimination of erythromycin from your body, potentially affecting its efficacy. Conversely, erythromycin may slow the removal of other drugs from your system, which could alter their effectiveness. Additionally, this medication may interfere with specific laboratory tests, such as urine tests, potentially leading to inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests may be conducted while you are taking this medication. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in July 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific needs. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice.
